coverage: The little-endian SET_SCANOUT wire fixture round-trips the header, rectangle, scanout id, and resource id.
A valid control-queue request binds resource 1 to scanout 0; a split 16+32-byte readable request is decoded across descriptors.
Resource id 0 disables scanout 0, including when its ignored rectangle contains extreme coordinates.
Short requests return ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER without changing the binding or queue progress.
The bounded attack matrix rejects scanout id 1, scanout id u32::MAX, unknown resource id u32::MAX, and overflowing rectangle coordinates while preserving the prior binding.
The default NullSink is constructed for headless devices and the FrameSink trait is kept in the core crate without browser dependencies.

virtio_regression.command: cargo test -p wasm-vm-core --test virtio_mmio_slots --test virtio_blk --test virtio_net_critic

claim: At commit c8ea5b0, SET_SCANOUT binds only an existing resource to the single valid scanout after checked rectangle validation, resource id 0 safely disables it, rejected requests preserve the prior binding, and the core exposes a browser-independent FrameSink boundary with a headless NullSink.
scope_notes: TRANSFER_TO_HOST_2D and RESOURCE_FLUSH behavior remain owned by E5-T03b and E5-T03c.
No independent-machine, WebKit, or host-layer rr run was used, per the user's direction and current repository evidence policy.
